Typical turbine-inlet temperatures are of the order of 1650 K (2500°F) or higher.
Typical heat fluxes in turbine blades are of the order of 5.5 x 10^6 watts per square meter.
Wall-to-coolant temperature ratios in turbine blades can be of the order of 2.5 to 1.
Rotational speeds for advanced large gas turbines can be of the order of 17,000 rpm, and for small turbines 65,000 rpm.
Acceleration levels for advanced large gas turbines can be of the order of 75,000 g's, and for small turbines 400,000 g's.
The Dittus-Boelter correlation can have errors of the order of 4% under the high temperature and heat flux conditions found in turbine blades.
The Petukhov-Popov correlation for constant physical properties in circular pipes has been used in addition to the Dittus-Boelter correlation.
Correlations have been developed that account for the effect of variable physical properties, showing that the heat transfer coefficient decreases as the wall-to-bulk temperature ratio increases.
Heat transfer in noncircular ducts is generally less than in circular ducts under the same conditions.
Pressure drop in noncircular ducts can be equal to or less than in circular ducts at constant property conditions, but greater at variable property conditions.
